prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the right contractor depends on your location, roof type, insurance situation, and schedule. I can help you find good options, but first here’s how to identify the best roofer for your specific job and avoid common scams.

How to pick the best hail-damage roofer
- Experience with hail claims: Look for contractors who work regularly with insurance companies and can document hail-specific repairs.
- Licensing & insurance: Verify Colorado contractor registration, current general liability and workers’ compensation insurance.
- Manufacturer certifications: Preferred/elite certifications from GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, etc. indicate training and extended warranties.
- Local reputation: Check recent Google, Yelp, Angi, and BBB reviews for hail-season work (last 12–24 months).
- Written estimates & scope: Get at least 3 written bids that list materials, brand/models, number of squares, removal vs overlay, decking repairs, ventilation, and warranty.
- Warranty & workmanship: Ask what’s covered, for how long, and whether they provide a workmanship warranty in addition to the shingle manufacturer warranty.
- Permits & inspection: They should handle city permits and coordinate final inspections.
- Payment & lien waivers: Avoid large up-front cash payments. Use milestone payments and require lien waivers when paid.
- Local crew vs storm-chaser: Prefer established Denver-area companies over out-of-state crews who follow storms (they often vanish after collecting deposits).

Red flags / things to avoid
- High-pressure “today only” pricing or insisting you sign immediately.
- Door-to-door solicitors claiming to be insurance-approved (insurers don’t approve specific contractors).
- No physical address, no local references, or only a P.O. box.
- Requests for full payment up-front in cash.

Questions to ask a roofer
- Are you licensed/registered in Colorado? Can you show insurance certificates?
- Are you certified by any shingle manufacturers? Which ones?
- Can you provide recent local references for hail repairs?
- Who will handle the insurance claim documentation and supplements?
- What is included in the written estimate and warranty?
- What is the project timeline and how will storm-related delays be handled?

Where to look
- Google Maps (search “hail damage roof repair Denver”), read top-reviewed listings.
- Angi, HomeAdvisor, BBB for accreditation and complaints.
- Colorado Roofing Association or local trade groups.
- Your insurer’s preferred/vendor list (still vet them).

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated local roofers near your ZIP code (I’ll find recent reviews and certifications).
- Provide a sample checklist/email to send to contractors to request bids.
Tell me your ZIP code and whether you’ve filed an insurance claim yet, and I’ll pull a short list of reputable local options.
